slot.brief: Helical motion: a charged particle enters at an angle to a uniform magnetic field; compute radius of the helix and time period of revolution, and compare with the perpendicular-entry case.

stem: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at $30^\circ$ to the field with speed $v$. Compared with entry at the same speed perpendicular to the field, what are the ratios of its helical radius and revolution period?

verdicts.working: The perpendicular speed is v sin 30° = v/2, so the helical-radius ratio is 1/2. The cyclotron period 2πm/(|q|B) is unchanged, giving a period ratio of 1.

working:
$r=\dfrac{mv\sin\theta}{|q|B},\quad T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{|q|B}$
$\dfrac{r_{30^\circ}}{r_{90^\circ}}=\sin30^\circ=\dfrac12$
$\dfrac{T_{30^\circ}}{T_{90^\circ}}=1$

Independent check: The perpendicular speed is v sin 30° = v/2, so the helical-radius ratio is 1/2. The cyclotron period 2πm/(|q|B) is unchanged, giving a period ratio of 1.
solution:
The helical radius depends on the perpendicular speed, while the cyclotron period is independent of speed:
$$r=\frac{mv\sin\theta}{|q|B},\qquad T=\frac{2\pi m}{|q|B}$$
Thus, $\dfrac{r_{30^\circ}}{r_{90^\circ}}=\sin30^\circ=\dfrac12$ and $\dfrac{T_{30^\circ}}{T_{90^\circ}}=1$.
